correctness.rationale: Variation-measure Minkowski reduction is exact; product-uniform Gamma survival gives every single-jump residual; its derivative is e^{-L}[1-2/(m-1)! integral_0^L y^{m-1}Q_m(y)dy], a strictly single-crossing function. Consequently all extremizers are the unique jump, and C_m=Q_m(L_m). The factorial benchmark, Chernoff lower-tail bound, dominated Gamma series and Stirling expansion prove the full sharp exponentially small squared deficit. Finite checker passed 188 assertions, but proof is analytic.

value.rationale: A natural all-iterate norm of a canonical positive integral operator has a unique extremizing discontinuity and a sharp exponential saturation law, including its unusual factorial-root localization and m^{-1/(2e)} prefactor. The result distinguishes large-iterate worst-case BV behavior from pointwise convergence and provides a genuinely structural benchmark rather than a small numerical cutoff.
